bibl.title: Agoranomische Urkunden aus Philadelpheia (P.Freib. 78 und 79)
bibl.seg: 141.4 P. Freib. Inv. 37 a = P. Freib. 79; Inv. 76 I = P. Freib. 78 145.4 P. Freib. III, 32-33; 42
François Gerardin, Stephan Neitmann & Lucas Weisser-Gericke, Agoranomische Urkunden aus Philadelpheia (P.Freib. 78 und 79).
bibl.note: Documents copied at the branch of the agoranomos's office in Philadelphia in the first half of the second century BCE. - P. Freib. Inv. 76 I = P. Freib. 78 [erste Hälfte des 2. Jh. v.Chr.] records a conciliation before the chrematistai, which comprised the official recording of the mutual concessions made by the parties as well as a memorandum to the judges. The attestation of an Atargateion, a private sanctuary dedicated to the "Syrian goddess", provides a link to P. Freib. III, 42 and suggests Philadelphia as the likely provenance of the piece. - P. Freib. Inv. 37 a = P. Freib. 79, on the other hand, were written in the same hand as P. Freib. III, 32-33, which provides a secure paleographical link with the agoranomic material from Philadelphia.
